record.paper_title: Current Open Questions in Complete Mixability
record.original_question: Is every absolutely continuous distribution supported on a bounded interval n-completely mixable once n is large enough?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7. Are all absolutely continuous distributions on a bounded interval n-CM for large enough n?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer. A probability distribution $F$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is called $n$-completely mixable ($n$-CM) if there exist random variables $X_1, X_2, \dots, X_n$, each with marginal distribution $F$, and a constant $c \in \mathbb{R}$ such that
$$ \mathbb{P}(X_1 + X_2 + \cdots + X_n = c) = 1. $$
(The joint distribution of $(X_1,\dots,X_n)$ is not required to be the product distribution; only the marginals are fixed to be $F$.)

Question: Let $F$ be any absolutely continuous probability distribution (with respect to Lebesgue measure) supported on a bounded interval $[a,b] \subset \mathbb{R}$. Is it true that there exists an integer $N = N(F)$ such that $F$ is $n$-completely mixable for every $n \ge N$?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted search did not surface any published resolution of this question. The problem is listed among the open questions in the survey on complete mixability, and known positive results in the literature cover restricted classes (e.g., distributions with concave or monotone densities, or bounded densities under additional hypotheses), but no general proof or counterexample for arbitrary absolutely continuous distributions on a bounded interval was found.

status_evidence.title: Current open questions in complete mixability
status_evidence.snippet: Open Problem 7. Are all absolutely continuous distributions on a bounded interval n-CM for large enough n?
status_evidence.claim: The question is recorded as an open problem in the complete mixability literature.

status_evidence.title: Advances in complete mixability
status_evidence.snippet: Continuous distributions with a concave density on a bounded interval are n-completely mixable for n sufficiently large.
status_evidence.claim: Only restricted classes (e.g., concave/monotone densities) are known to be asymptotically completely mixable.
